heroHeadline: JT-60SA Restarts; TAE/UKAEA Launch Commercial JV; China Elevates Fusion in 15th Five-Year Plan
heroSubtitle: On May 15, the world's largest operational superconducting tokamak — JT-60SA in Naka, Japan — completed a comprehensive upgrade programme and began integrated commissioning under new project leader Jerónimo García, with plasma heating experiments planned for late 2026. On May 14, TAE Technologies and UKAEA formally launched TAE Beam UK, a joint venture at Culham Campus commercializing neutral beam and accelerator technology for food safety, cancer therapy, and homeland security — converting fusion R&D into near-term revenue. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) designates fusion as one of eight national frontier technology priorities, backed by $6.5B+ in government investment since 2023 and new facilities including the BEST tokamak under construction. Also highlighted: Jefferson Lab's $29M DOE spin-polarized fusion fuel research, which could boost D-T fusion yield efficiency by up to 80% if validated at scale.
footerNote: Data sourced from DOE/LLNL/NNSA, ITER Organization, Commonwealth Fusion Systems, ARPA-E, UK Government, Fusion for Energy, ANS Nuclear Newswire, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Physical Review Letters, Fusion Science and Technology), and the Fusion Industry Association.
